issues.t: Engine stalls or dies while driving
issues.sym: The engine cuts out at stop signs, in turns or while merging onto the highway, sometimes with the battery or check engine light flashing. Power steering and brake assist go heavy, and it may take several tries to restart.
issues.why: Most reports involve the 2.4L engine. Low oil from oil burning is a common finding, and some cars needed engine computer updates or electrical repairs; a few had internal engine damage and got a new engine.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Check the oil level right away and keep it full. Ask the dealer about software updates and have the oil consumption, battery and charging system tested. Report repeated stalling to NHTSA.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: You have to add a quart of oil every 500-1,000 miles, the dipstick reads low between changes, and in some cases the engine stalls, rattles or smells burnt.
issues.why: The 2.4L Tigershark engine can burn oil internally; one dealer found scored cylinder walls. Some cars got replacement engines under the powertrain warranty.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up. Ask the dealer for an oil consumption test and keep records, as they may support a warranty or goodwill engine repair.

issues.t: Automatic transmission stops working or goes into limp mode
issues.sym: A 'service transmission' light, the car dropping into neutral or refusing to engage a gear, limp mode with low speed, rough shifts or grinding.
issues.why: Causes reported include failed transmission computers and valve bodies, broken shift cable brackets or linkage, poor ground connections and internal failure. Two recalls also cover a shift cable bushing and a transmission computer fault.
issues.next: Get it to a safe place and have codes read before agreeing to a new transmission. Check your VIN for the shifter cable and transmission computer recalls first.

issues.t: Jerky or rough shifting from the dual-clutch automatic
issues.sym: Jerky take-offs, hesitation, harsh or delayed shifts and a jumpy feel at low speed in stop-and-go traffic.
issues.why: The 1.4L turbo was paired with a dual dry-clutch automated manual, which reviewers flag as the most trouble-prone transmission in the Dart.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about transmission software updates and have the clutch adaptation checked. If buying used, test-drive it in traffic.

issues.t: Clutch pedal sticks to the floor (manual)
issues.sym: On manual-transmission cars the clutch pedal stays down or sticks, you can't shift, and the car may stall. It comes and goes and can be worse in heat.
issues.why: The clutch hydraulic system (master cylinder and line to the slave cylinder) loses pressure. A Chrysler service bulletin added a new-style master cylinder and line.
issues.next: Pull over safely if it happens. Ask the dealer about the clutch master cylinder service bulletin; a full clutch replacement may not be needed.

issues.t: Turbocharger failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, knocking from the engine bay, poor or on-and-off acceleration, a noisy turbo or white smoke.
issues.why: The 1.4L turbo or its control sensor and solenoid fail, sometimes at low mileage.
issues.next: Use the correct 5W-40 synthetic oil and change it on time. Have the turbo control parts tested before replacing the whole turbo; ask about warranty coverage.

issues.t: Engine revs up while stopped with foot on the brake
issues.sym: While stopped, the engine suddenly revs high, sometimes to redline, and the car feels like it wants to move.
issues.why: No single cause has been confirmed; most reports involve the 1.4L turbo with the automatic. Dealers often couldn't reproduce it.
issues.next: Hold the brake firmly and shift to neutral if it happens. Document each event, report it to NHTSA and ask the dealer for software updates.

issues.t: Check engine light from misfires and ignition coils
issues.sym: The check engine light comes and goes, sometimes flashing, with rough running or a misfire on one cylinder.
issues.why: Failed ignition coils, sensors and wiring are common causes. Chrysler also issued an engine computer update for several codes on 2013-2015 2.4L cars.
issues.next: A flashing light means stop driving hard and get it checked soon. Have the codes read; a coil is a fairly simple fix.

issues.t: Thermostat failure turns on check engine light
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on (often code P0128), especially in cold weather, and the heater may be slow to warm up.
issues.why: The thermostat sticks open so the engine doesn't reach normal temperature. An engine computer update may also be needed.
issues.next: Not urgent, but get it fixed so the engine and heater work properly. Ask the dealer whether a software update applies.

issues.t: Coolant leak and overheating
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs, a coolant warning appears, and you may see coolant under the car or smell it.
issues.why: Coolant leaks, often from a heater hose, let the level drop until the 2.0L engine overheats.
issues.next: Stop if the gauge goes into the red. Check the coolant level often and have any leak fixed quickly to avoid head gasket damage.

issues.t: Oil pressure sensor sets check engine light
issues.sym: Check engine light with code P0520, with no real oil pressure problem.
issues.why: A faulty oil pressure sensor. Chrysler service bulletin 18-034-14 calls for replacing the sensor.
issues.next: Check the oil level first to rule out a real problem, then have the sensor replaced.

issues.t: Wipers stay on or won't shut off
issues.sym: The windshield wipers keep running or don't respond properly to the switch.
issues.why: A flat ribbon wire inside the steering column control module (SCCM) fails.
issues.next: Have a dealer or experienced shop do it, because the airbag and steering wheel must come off. The module may need programming.

issues.t: Uconnect screen goes blank or radio shuts off
issues.sym: The touchscreen goes blank, the radio shuts off or resets, Bluetooth won't connect, or the backup camera display fails.
issues.why: Software glitches in the Uconnect system. Chrysler released updates, and some faults clear after a reset.
issues.next: Install the latest Uconnect software update. Disconnecting the battery briefly can reset it; a dealer can replace the unit if it keeps failing.

issues.t: Creaking or squeaking when turning
issues.sym: A creak or squeak from the front when turning the steering wheel, especially at low speeds.
issues.why: The upper strut mounts dry out and bind. Chrysler service bulletin 02-004-15 covers lubricating them.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to apply the strut mount service bulletin. It is not a safety problem but should be checked if it gets worse.

issues.t: Sun visor breaks and hangs down
issues.sym: The sun visor snaps at the hinge and dangles, sometimes by its wires, which can also knock out the interior lights.
issues.why: The plastic around the visor hinge is brittle and cracks with normal use.
issues.next: Replacement visors are easy to install. Ask the dealer if your car is still under warranty.

issues.t: Steering binds or becomes very heavy
issues.sym: The steering wheel catches, binds or suddenly takes a lot of force to turn, sometimes with a cracking sound from the column.
issues.why: Owners report it on low-mileage cars; no cause has been confirmed.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. This is a safety issue. Have the steering system inspected right away and report it to NHTSA.

issues.t: Shifter cable can come off the transmission (recall)
issues.sym: The gear you pick doesn't match what the car does, or the car can roll away after you select Park.
issues.why: The bushing that holds the shifter cable to the 6-speed automatic can fail. Recall 19V-293 covers 2013-2016 Darts with that transmission.
issues.next: Always use the parking brake until the recall is done. Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov/recalls; the dealer replaces the bushing for free.

issues.t: Transmission can shift into neutral (recall)
issues.sym: The car suddenly loses drive as the transmission drops into neutral.
issues.why: The transmission control module can fail. Recall 15V-542 replaces the module and its bracket on cars built from 2012 to mid-2015.
issues.next: Check your VIN for this recall; the repair is free.

issues.t: Oil can damage the brake booster (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal gets harder to press and the car takes longer to stop.
issues.why: Oil from the engine's vacuum pump can seep into the brake booster and damage it, reducing brake assist. Recall 15V-800.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. If the pedal feels hard, get it checked right away. Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the vacuum line, and the booster and pump too if oil is found.

issues.t: Wipers can stop working from washer pump fault (recall)
issues.sym: The windshield wipers stop working.
issues.why: Voltage spikes from a faulty washer pump can knock out the wiper circuit on 2016 cars built from April 2015 to June 2016. Recall 16V-813.
issues.next: Check your VIN; the dealer replaces the washer pump for free.
